query: FCC high-entropy alloys lose substantial strength above 800 °C, motivating refractory high-entropy alloys. Equal-atomic, single-phase BCC NbMoTaW retains excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but has poor room-temperature ductility, and its irradiation resistance has been inferred computationally rather than established here experimentally. Studies of other refractory high-entropy alloys have found greater irradiation resistance than pure tungsten under helium implantation and self-healing behavior associated with enhanced atomic diffusion and redistribution. However, irradiation-induced amorphization, helium-energy-dependent blistering, and irradiation-enhanced precipitation have also been observed, indicating unresolved phase- and surface-stability risks. Given the need to preserve BCC structural stability and high-temperature mechanical performance while improving room-temperature ductility and irradiation tolerance, what intervention could achieve this balance? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted directional or quantitative outcomes relative to untreated NbMoTaW, the applicable temperature and irradiation boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Trace interstitial boron (0.05–0.2 at.% total) introduced into equiatomic NbMoTaW will segregate to grain boundaries, thereby (a) increasing room-temperature tensile ductility and (b) acting as preferential sinks for irradiation-generated point defects and implanted He, while (c) leaving the single-phase BCC solid-solution and its high-temperature strength essentially unchanged.
generation.material_initial_state: Arc-melted, homogenized, equiatomic single-phase BCC NbMoTaW polycrystal with grain size 20–50 µm and <0.01 at.% interstitial impurities.
generation.intervention: Add 0.05–0.2 at.% boron during alloy melting followed by identical homogenization (e.g., 1800 °C, 24 h, vacuum) and grain-size control heat treatment.
generation.conditions: Mechanical tests at 25 °C and 1600 °C; 1–3 dpa self-ion or 10 MeV He irradiation at 800 °C (flux 10⁻⁴–10⁻³ dpa s⁻¹).
generation.structural_mediator: Boron-decorated grain boundaries and sub-grain dislocation networks within the BCC solid solution.
generation.mechanism: 1. Boron segregation lowers the grain-boundary excess free volume and enhances cohesion, delaying intergranular crack initiation and permitting easier dislocation transmission, which raises elongation to failure. 2. The high binding energy between B and vacancies/interstitials creates recombination sites and heterogeneous traps for He, reducing bubble nucleation and growth. 3. The B concentration is below the solubility limit, so lattice parameter, solid-solution strengthening, and high-temperature creep resistance remain dominated by Nb–Mo–Ta–W interactions.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to undoped NbMoTaW: • Room-temperature total elongation will at least double (e.g., from ~2 % to ≥5 %) at similar 0.2 % yield strength (within ±10 %). • After 2 dpa He irradiation at 800 °C, nano-bubble density will be ≥50 % lower and mean bubble radius ≤70 % of baseline. • 0.2 % yield strength at 1600 °C will drop by <5 %.
generation.baseline: Undoped equiatomic NbMoTaW subjected to identical thermo-mechanical history and irradiation dose.
generation.boundary: Effect expected as long as boron remains below ~0.3 at.% (to avoid boride precipitation) and test temperature is ≤1600 °C; above this or if B forms stable borides, predicted benefits diminish.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of ductility improvement and bubble-density reduction is estimated; actual values may vary with grain size and exact B level. Excessive B may form NbB or TaB precipitates, altering outcomes.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two alloys: (i) NbMoTaW (baseline) and (ii) NbMoTaW-0.1 B (intervention). Homogenize identically. Perform: a) uniaxial tensile tests at 25 °C, strain rate 1×10⁻³ s⁻¹; b) identical tests at 1600 °C; c) He⁺ irradiation to 2 dpa at 800 °C followed by TEM bubble counting.
measurements: 0.2 % yield strength and total elongation at 25 °C and 1600 °C
Post-irradiation bubble density (bubbles m⁻³) and mean radius (nm) via TEM
XRD/EBSD confirmation of single-phase BCC after processing
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if any of the following hold: (1) Room-temperature elongation of the B-doped alloy is ≤ baseline value +1 % absolute; (2) He-bubble density is reduced by <20 % OR mean radius reduction <10 % compared to baseline; (3) 0.2 % yield strength at 1600 °C decreases by >10 % relative to baseline.
